title: The Mystery of the Humming Machine
summary: A curious girl and the community center's engineer track down a strange, steady hum behind a locked door and discover a tired old water-filtration machine that just needs one worn part replaced.
poll: A strange sound usually has a plain, ordinary explanation once someone looks closely.

versions.title: The Humming Machine
versions.text:
Noor hears a hum. It comes from a locked room. The room is at the center.

Noor wants to know why. She asks at the desk. No one knows.

Noor meets Mr. Omar. He fixes things at the center. He has a key for each room.

"I hear it too," he says. "Let's go look."

They open the door. A big old thing hums inside. It feels hot.

"This cleans the water," says Mr. Omar. "It is for the pool and the sinks."

One small part broke. That is why it hums so loud.

Mr. Omar gets a new part. They put it in. The hum stops!

Noor smiles. It was not scary at all. It was just a tired old thing.

versions.title: The Humming Machine

Noor wants to know why. She asks the lady at the desk, but no one seems to know.

Then Noor meets Mr. Omar, who fixes things at the center. He has a key that opens each room.

"I hear that hum too," he says with a smile. "Let's go look at it together."

They open the heavy door. A big old thing sits inside, humming loud and feeling hot.

"This thing cleans our water," says Mr. Omar. "It cleans water for the pool and the sinks."

The thing has worked too hard. One small part has broken, and that is why it hums so loud.

Mr. Omar gets a new part and brings it back. They put it in together. The hum stops at last!

Noor smiles with relief. It was not scary at all. It was just a tired old thing that needed help.

versions.title: The Mystery of the Humming Machine
versions.text:
Noor hears a strange, steady hum echoing somewhere inside the community center. The odd sound seems to drift from a locked room right next to the swimming pool.

Noor is extremely curious about what could be making such a noise. She asks the woman at the front desk, but even she has no idea what it could be.

Then Noor happens to meet Mr. Omar, the center's engineer, in the hallway. He carries a large ring of keys that can unlock every room in the building.

"I have actually heard that hum too," says Mr. Omar with a friendly smile. "Let's go find out exactly what it is together."

They unlock the heavy door and step carefully into the small, warm room. A big, old machine sits right in the middle, humming loudly and vibrating slightly against the floor.

"This machine filters all of our water," Mr. Omar explains patiently. "It cleans the water that flows to the drinking fountains and to the swimming pool."

The machine, it turns out, has been running almost nonstop lately, especially since the center hosted a large event last week. One small part inside has worn out from the extra strain, and that is exactly why it hums so loudly now.

Mr. Omar quickly orders a replacement part and brings it back the next morning. Together, they remove the old part and install the new one. Suddenly, the loud humming finally stops!

Noor smiles with relief. The strange mystery was never a monster at all. It was simply a hardworking old machine that needed one small part replaced.

One small but essential part called a bearing, which helps a moving part spin smoothly, has worn out completely, and that is exactly why the machine hums so loudly now.

Mr. Omar quickly orders a brand-new replacement bearing and brings it back the very next morning. Together, they carefully remove the old, worn-out part and install the new one. Suddenly, the loud humming noise finally stops completely!

Noor smiles with relief and genuine excitement. The strange mystery was never a monster or anything scary at all. It was simply a hardworking old machine that just needed one small, important part replaced.

versions.title: The Mystery of the Humming Machine
versions.text:
Noor hears a strange, persistent hum echoing somewhere within the community center, a sound that seems to drift from a locked room situated beside the swimming pool, never appearing to stop regardless of the hour, a peculiarity that only deepens the mystery surrounding it and that has begun to occupy her thoughts throughout the day.

Noor eventually encounters Mr. Omar, the center's building engineer, in the hallway outside the pool area, after the woman at the front desk admits, with an apologetic shrug, that she has no genuine idea what could be producing such an unusual, unrelenting sound; he carries a large, heavy ring of keys capable of unlocking every single room in the building, from storage closets to mechanical rooms hidden deep in the basement.

"I have actually heard that hum myself," says Mr. Omar with a friendly smile, setting down the clipboard he had been carrying. "Let's go investigate exactly what it is together, shall we?" They unlock the heavy metal door and step carefully into the small, warm room beyond it, where a large, aging machine sits in the middle of the space, humming loudly and vibrating slightly against the concrete floor beneath their feet.

"This machine filters all of our water," Mr. Omar explains patiently, raising his voice slightly over the noise. "Filtration removes dirt, microscopic particles, and harmful germs from the water flowing to the drinking fountains and the swimming pool, thereby keeping every visitor healthy and safe." The machine, it turns out, has been operating almost continuously lately, especially since the center hosted a large community event the previous week that drew far more visitors than usual.

A small but essential component called a bearing, which allows a moving part to spin smoothly without excess friction, has worn out entirely from the additional strain placed upon it, and that is precisely why the machine hums so loudly now; Mr. Omar promptly orders a brand-new replacement bearing and brings it back the very next morning, eager to resolve the problem before it worsens further.

Together, they carefully remove the old, worn-out component and install the new one, tightening every bolt with methodical care, and suddenly the loud humming noise finally stops completely, leaving the room in an unfamiliar, almost startling silence.

Noor smiles with relief and genuine excitement; the strange mystery was never a monster or anything frightening at all, for it was simply a hardworking old machine that needed one small, important component replaced. Now she understands precisely how the center keeps its water clean and safe for everyone who visits, a realization that fills her with quiet, lasting pride in engineering as a profession worth considering.

versions.title: The Mystery of the Humming Machine
versions.text:
Noor hears a strange, persistent hum echoing somewhere within the community center, a sound that seems to drift from a locked room situated beside the swimming pool, and it never appears to stop, regardless of the hour, a peculiarity that only deepens the mystery surrounding it and that lingers unresolved in the back of her mind for most of the afternoon.

Noor eventually encounters Mr. Omar, the center's building engineer, in the hallway outside the pool area, after the woman at the front desk admits, somewhat apologetically, that she has no genuine idea what could be producing such an unrelenting, unusual sound; he carries a large, heavy ring of keys capable of unlocking virtually every room in the building, from storage closets to mechanical rooms situated deep in the basement.

"I have actually heard that hum myself," says Mr. Omar with a friendly smile, pausing his inspection of a nearby panel. "Let's go investigate exactly what it is together, shall we?" They unlock the heavy metal door and step carefully into the small, warm room beyond it, where a large, aging machine sits in the middle of the space, humming loudly and vibrating noticeably against the concrete floor beneath them.

"This machine filters all of our water," Mr. Omar explains patiently, speaking a little louder than usual over the noise. "Filtration systematically removes dirt, microscopic particles, and harmful microorganisms from the water flowing to the drinking fountains and the swimming pool, thereby keeping every visitor healthy and safe." The machine, it transpires, has been operating almost continuously of late, especially since the center hosted a large community event the previous week that strained every system in the building.

A small but essential component called a bearing, which enables a moving part to rotate smoothly without excessive friction, has deteriorated entirely from the additional mechanical strain, and that is precisely why the machine hums so loudly now; Mr. Omar promptly orders a brand-new replacement bearing and retrieves it the very next morning, determined to have the machine running quietly again by the afternoon.

Together, they methodically remove the deteriorated component and install the replacement, tightening every bolt with painstaking care, and suddenly the persistent humming noise finally ceases completely, leaving the room in an unfamiliar, almost disorienting silence.

Noor smiles with relief and genuine excitement; the strange mystery was never a monster or anything frightening whatsoever, for it was simply a hardworking, overworked machine that required one small, essential component to be replaced. Now she comprehends precisely how the center preserves its water as clean and safe for everyone who visits, a realization that instills in her a quiet, lasting pride in the discipline of engineering and a genuine curiosity about how such systems are designed.

versions.title: The Mystery of the Humming Machine
versions.text:
Noor hears a strange, persistent hum echoing somewhere within the community center, a sound drifting from a locked room beside the swimming pool that never appears to stop regardless of the hour, a peculiarity that only deepens the mystery surrounding it, until she eventually encounters Mr. Omar, the center's building engineer, in the hallway outside the pool area.

The woman at the front desk had already admitted she had no genuine idea what could be producing such an unrelenting sound, so Noor is relieved when Mr. Omar, carrying a large, heavy ring of keys capable of unlocking virtually every room in the building, says with a friendly smile, "I have actually heard that hum myself. Let's go investigate exactly what it is together, shall we?"

They unlock the heavy metal door and step carefully into the small, warm room beyond it, where a large, aging machine sits in the middle of the space, humming loudly and vibrating noticeably against the concrete floor; Mr. Omar explains patiently that this machine filters all of the center's water, systematically removing dirt, microscopic particles, and harmful microorganisms from the water flowing to the drinking fountains and the swimming pool, thereby keeping every visitor healthy and safe.

The machine, it transpires, has been operating almost continuously of late, especially since the center hosted a large community event the previous week, and a small but essential component called a bearing, which enables a moving part to rotate smoothly without excessive friction, has deteriorated entirely from the additional mechanical strain—precisely why the machine hums so loudly now.

Mr. Omar promptly orders a brand-new replacement bearing and retrieves it the very next morning, and together they methodically remove the deteriorated component and install the replacement, tightening every bolt with painstaking care, until the persistent humming noise finally ceases completely, leaving the room in unfamiliar silence.

Noor smiles with relief and genuine excitement, for the strange mystery was never a monster or anything frightening whatsoever; it was simply a hardworking, overworked machine that required one small, essential component to be replaced, and now she comprehends precisely how the center preserves its water as clean and safe for everyone who visits, a realization that instills in her a quiet, lasting pride in the discipline of engineering.

In the days that follow, Noor returns to the mechanical room several times, asking Mr. Omar an increasing number of questions about pumps, filters, and the way a single worn bearing could cause such an alarming noise throughout the building, and he patiently answers every one, clearly pleased by her curiosity. By the end of the month, she has started keeping a small notebook of everything she has learned, and she tells her parents, somewhat shyly, that she might like to become an engineer herself one day, inspired by an ordinary machine that turned out to have a perfectly ordinary explanation.

versions.title: The Mystery of the Humming Machine
versions.text:
Noor hears a strange, persistent hum echoing somewhere within the community center, a sound drifting from a locked room beside the swimming pool that never appears to stop regardless of the hour, a peculiarity that only deepens the mystery surrounding it, until she eventually encounters Mr. Omar, the center's building engineer, in the hallway outside the pool area, where he happens to be reviewing a maintenance schedule.

The woman at the front desk had already admitted she had no genuine idea what could be producing such an unrelenting sound, so Noor is relieved when Mr. Omar, carrying a large, heavy ring of keys capable of unlocking virtually every room in the building, says with a friendly smile, "I have actually heard that hum myself. Let's go investigate exactly what it is together, shall we?"

They unlock the heavy metal door and step carefully into the small, warm room beyond it, where a large, aging machine sits in the middle of the space, humming loudly and vibrating noticeably against the concrete floor; Mr. Omar explains patiently that this machine filters all of the center's water, systematically removing dirt, microscopic particles, and harmful microorganisms from the water flowing to the drinking fountains and the swimming pool, thereby keeping every visitor healthy and safe throughout the year.

The machine, it transpires, has been operating almost continuously of late, especially since the center hosted a large community event the previous week, and a small but essential component called a bearing, which enables a moving part to rotate smoothly without excessive friction, has deteriorated entirely from the additional mechanical strain—precisely why the machine hums so loudly now, a fact Mr. Omar diagnoses within minutes of listening to it.

Mr. Omar promptly orders a brand-new replacement bearing and retrieves it the very next morning, and together they methodically remove the deteriorated component and install the replacement, tightening every bolt with painstaking care, until the persistent humming noise finally ceases completely, leaving the room in unfamiliar silence.

Noor smiles with relief and genuine excitement, for the strange mystery was never a monster or anything frightening whatsoever; it was simply a hardworking, overworked machine that required one small, essential component to be replaced, and now she comprehends precisely how the center preserves its water as clean and safe for everyone who visits, a realization that instills in her a quiet, lasting pride in the discipline of engineering and a desire to learn more about it herself.

In the weeks that follow, Noor returns to the mechanical room again and again, peppering Mr. Omar with an ever-growing list of questions about pumps, filters, bearings, and the countless small parts that quietly keep the entire building running, and he answers each question with evident delight at her curiosity. By the time the next community event arrives, she has filled an entire notebook with diagrams and notes, and she has quietly decided, without telling anyone just yet, that she wants to study engineering when she is older, all because of one humming machine that turned out to have nothing mysterious about it at all.

questions.stem: What is this story mainly about?
options: A girl and a helper find out why a locked room keeps making a hum
A girl who gets lost inside a very big building
A pool that closes down for the whole long summer
A machine that can talk and tell silly jokes
questions.why: The story follows Noor and Mr. Omar as they find out what is making the strange hum behind the locked door.

wrong.B: Noor is never shown getting lost in the building.
wrong.C: The pool stays open the whole time in this story.
wrong.D: The old machine hums, but it never talks or jokes.

questions.stem: What happens right after Noor asks the desk and no one knows about the hum?

Mr. Omar locks the door again right away

turns the color of the water bright blue

questions.why: Installing the new bearing happens near the very end, right before the humming finally stops.

wrong.C: Noticing the hum is the very first event.

questions.stem: Why has the machine been working much too hard lately?

Mr. Omar forgot to turn it off at night
The center hosted a large event the week before
The drinking fountains were all removed

wrong.A: Pool cleaning is never mentioned as the reason.
wrong.B: Mr. Omar forgetting to turn it off is not stated.
wrong.D: The drinking fountains are still working, not removed.

questions.stem: In the story, the word filter most nearly means to —
options: make a sound much louder than before
lock a heavy metal door tightly shut
clean a liquid by removing unwanted material
add a lot more water into a full pool
questions.why: The machine filters water by removing dirt and particles, meaning it cleans the water of unwanted material.

wrong.A: Filtering has nothing to do with loudness.
wrong.B: Locking a door is unrelated to the word filter.
wrong.D: Adding water is not what filtering means here.

questions.stem: What can you infer about why Mr. Omar can fix the hum so quickly?
options: As the center's engineer, he knows how its machines work
He built the entire community center all by himself
He has honestly never heard a machine hum before
He simply asks Noor to repair the machine herself

wrong.C: Mr. Omar says he has heard a hum like this before.
wrong.D: Mr. Omar does the repair himself, with Noor watching.

questions.stem: What does the worn-out bearing suggest about machines that run for a very long time without rest?
options: They always seem to run better the longer they work
Their parts can wear out and may need to be replaced
They never need to have any of their parts replaced
They stop making absolutely any sound at all
questions.why: Running almost nonstop wore out the bearing, showing that overworked machine parts can wear out and need replacing.

wrong.A: Running longer wore the part out, not improved it.
wrong.C: The bearing does need to be replaced in this story.
wrong.D: The overworked machine makes a very loud sound, not silence.

questions.stem: How is Noor's curiosity about the hum similar to Mr. Omar's job as an engineer?
options: Neither one of them actually cares about finding an answer
Only Mr. Omar truly wants to solve this strange mystery
Both of them want to find the cause of a problem and fix it
Both of them dislike working inside the mechanical room
questions.why: Noor's curiosity and Mr. Omar's engineering work both lead them to investigate the cause of the hum and solve it.

wrong.B: Noor also wants to solve the mystery, not just Mr. Omar.
wrong.D: Neither one shows any dislike for the mechanical room.

questions.stem: Why does the author explain exactly how the filtering machine works?
options: To convince readers to stay away from swimming pools
To make the overall story much shorter to read
To hide the real cause of the hum from readers
To help readers understand the real reason behind the mystery

wrong.B: The explanation adds detail rather than shortening the story.
wrong.C: The explanation reveals the cause rather than hiding it.

keyWords.definition: one of the separate parts that make up a larger machine or system
keyWords.example: A single loose component inside the engine caused the whole car to stall.

keyWords.definition: a part that lets another part turn or slide smoothly, reducing friction
keyWords.example: A worn bearing in the fan made it squeak every time it spun.

keyWords.definition: continuing to happen or exist without stopping
keyWords.example: A persistent cough kept the whole family awake most of the night.

keyWords.definition: having to do with machines or the moving parts inside them
keyWords.example: The elevator stopped working because of a mechanical problem.

keyWords.definition: the force that slows down two surfaces rubbing against each other
keyWords.example: Oil reduces the friction between a bicycle chain and its gears.

questions.stem: Which statement best captures the central idea of this story?
options: A persistent hum at a center turns out to have a mechanical cause, sparking a girl's interest in engineering
A community center closes down permanently because of one strange noise
An engineer firmly refuses to investigate an unusual sound at all
A machine in a locked room is revealed to be somehow alive

wrong.B: The center stays open throughout the entire story.

wrong.D: The explanation is entirely mechanical, never anything alive.

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly orders these events from the story?

questions.stem: What is the underlying mechanical cause of the persistent humming?

wrong.B: Draining the pool is not given as a cause.
wrong.D: Mr. Omar does not misadjust any settings in the story.

questions.stem: In this story, the word component most nearly refers to —

a loud sound the machine makes while running
a trained person who repairs machines for work
one of the individual parts inside a larger machine

wrong.B: The humming sound is separate from the word component.

questions.stem: Based on the story, what can be inferred about why Mr. Omar diagnoses the problem so quickly?
options: His experience as an engineer helps him recognize familiar signs
He had secretly broken the machine himself earlier that week

questions.stem: What does Noor's growing habit of asking Mr. Omar questions suggest about her?

A monster story always ends with a mechanical explanation too
Unlike a monster story, this mystery ends with a plain, factual cause
